question: Road hogging

options.text: Ensures a smoother flow of traffic.
Causes other vehicles to overtake dangerously on the left.
Causes other vehicles to overtake on the right.

question: When you are caught in a traffic jam on an expressway, you should

options.text: Use the road shoulder to move in front.
Weave in and out of traffic to get in front.
Stay in your lane until traffic flow resumes.

question: What should you do if your brakes were slack or spongy?

options.text: Ignore them as long as it is effective.
Get them checked as soon as possible.
Pumps the brake before stopping.

notes: Source grammar kept as printed: option A 'them ... it is effective'; option C 'Pumps' (not 'Pump').

question: To stop your vehicle safely on a wet road, you should

options.text: Apply the foot brake followed by the hand brake.
Use your brakes gently and early.
Use engine brake only.

question: What can cause your tyres to skid and lose their grip on the road surface?

options.text: Heavy braking.
Looking over your shoulder.
Giving hand signals.

question: You are following learners who stalls at a junction. You should

options.text: Stay very close behind and flash your headlights.
Be patient as you expect them to make mistakes.
Immediately overtake them.

notes: Source grammar kept as printed: 'learners who stalls'.

question: On the expressway, you may ONLY stop on the road shoulder

options.text: If you feel tired and need to rest.
To pick up passengers.
In an emergency.

question: You are following a cyclist on an uneven road. You should

options.text: Overtake immediately.
Allow extra room in case they swerve to avoid pot-holes.
Follow closely so you can be seen in their mirrors.

question: You give road signals in order to

options.text: Help other car drivers only.
Warn heavy vehicles only.
Warn and help all road users including pedestrians.

question: When moving off from a stationary position, what must you do first?

options.text: Check the road in front and behind you.
Move off then check for traffic on the right.
Tap the horn to warn other road users.

question: Why should you look out particularly for motorcyclists and cyclists at junctions?

options.text: They might want to turn into the side road.
They are harder to see.
They might not see you turn.

question: You are waiting to come out of a side road. Why should you watch carefully for motocycles?

options.text: Motorcycles have right of way.
Motorcycles are small and hard to see.
Motorcycles are usually faster than cars.

notes: Source typo kept: 'motocycles' in the question (options spell 'Motorcycles').

question: You are travelling along an expressway . You decided that you need a rest, you should

options.text: Stop on the road shoulder.
Leave at the next exit.
Park on the slip road.

notes: Source has a space before the full stop: 'expressway .'

question: You should adjust your __________so that all controls can be reached without having to stretch.

options.text: Seat belt
Eye-sight
Driver seat

notes: Question contains a fill-in blank drawn as an underline (length approximated with 10 underscores); no space between the blank and 'so'. Options have no final full stop.

question: Which wheels turn when you turn the steering wheel?

options.text: The front wheels.
The back wheels.
Both the front and back wheels.

question: While driving and your windscreen is shattered, you should

options.text: Apply emergency brake to stop immediately.
Slow down and stop at the road side to remove the shattered screen.
Drive at normal speed to a workshop.

question: When the amber light flashes continuously and there is a policeman standing in the middle of the junction, you should

options.text: Proceed on as the light is going to change.
Proceed on and give way to traffic on the right only.
Be cautious and follow the direction given by the policeman.

question: Which of the following statement on alcohol is true?

options.text: You may decline a breath or blood test.
Alcohol will not be detected by the breath test after peppermints have been eaten.
